result.answer:
Based on the site’s claims section, here's the answer:

**Yes — you have to pay the ¥12,000 assessment fee again for this second claim.**

**The rule**, from the Fee Schedule and FAQ pages:

- Fee Schedule (`/claims/fees/`): *"The claim assessment fee is ¥12,000, payable when the claim is lodged... The fee is waived entirely for repeat claimants — see fee waivers in the FAQ."*

- FAQ (`/claims/faq/#fee-waivers`): *"Claimants with two or more approved claims from separate incidents within any rolling 12-month period are exempt from the ¥12,000 assessment fee... The waiver counts approved claims only. Refused, withdrawn and pending claims do not count toward the two-claim threshold."*

**Why this doesn't help you yet:** The waiver only kicks in once you already have **two or more approved** claims from separate incidents. Right now you have just **one** approved claim (the March incident). The claim you're about to file — for the incident three weeks ago — is itself still *pending*, and the rule explicitly says pending claims don't count toward the two-claim threshold. So this second claim can't "waive itself."

In practice: you'll pay the ¥12,000 fee again when you lodge this second claim. If it is subsequently approved, you would then have two approved claims from separate incidents within the rolling 12-month window — meaning any *third* claim within that window would qualify for the automatic fee waiver (no separate application needed, per the FAQ).

One consolation from the same fee schedule: *"The assessment fee is refunded in full where the final award exceeds ¥1,000,000,"* so if your damage this time is substantial, you may get the fee back that way even though the repeat-claimant waiver doesn't apply yet.

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.

These three were ADDED AFTER defects were found in this scorer, not designed in from the start. Each one existed because a check had already scored an answer wrongly, and the last of them changed a finding that had already been handed over. They are listed so a reader can judge the instrument, including its history.

Answer text is normalised before matching: NFKC, Unicode dashes folded to "-", non-breaking spaces to " ", curly quotes to straight, and markdown emphasis markers removed. A model that writes "rolling 12‑month" or "only **one** approved" is making the same claim as one that does not.
A conclusion is read from position, not vocabulary: a correct answer quotes the rule it applies, so waiver wording inside a quotation does not outrank an explicit finding stated earlier.
Affirmative phrases are only counted when not negated within the preceding ~28 characters, so "should not have to pay" is not read as "have to pay".
